method: Read on 2026-11-13 from the per-shard text cache (~/.cache/dhvani/indicvoices_hindi_text/, built by load_indicvoices_text_rows at df63af1). Aadhaar/PAN pairs supported only by the bare Devanagari variants आधार / पैन were split by context; 20 random contexts per class were read by Claude. Government use-case tasks = task_name in {Aadhaar, PAN, Digilocker, Umang Commands, Health Services, Passport Seva, ITR Services, Gas Booking, NPS}. Awaiting owner confirmation.

bare_aadhaar_basis_pattern_pairs.verdict: false: every match is followed by ' पर' or preceded by 'के ' ('on the basis of'); all 20 samples read were the noun 'basis'

bare_aadhaar_other_pairs.verdict: gov-task samples all genuine ('मेरा आधार नंबर', 'आधार बायोमेट्रिक्स'); other-task samples mixed: some genuine ('आधार कार्', 'आधार पैन कार्ड चाहिए'), some 'basis' outside the pattern ('उसी आधार', 'आधार बनाना'), one 'उद्योग आधार' (a different government ID)

bare_pan_pairs.verdict: almost all false: 'पैन किलर' (pain killer), frying pan, pen; genuine only in ITR Services

caveats: The government use-case subset is 94% read speech (1304/1386 pairs). Read prompts are easier for ASR than spontaneous speech, so any EER measured on it is a lower bound on real-call error, and must be reported as such.

Only 9 government pairs are in the valid split; the eval must sample from train. Nothing is trained here, so that is legitimate, but IndicVoices train may be in Sarvam Saaras' training data: Saaras numbers on it are potentially in-distribution / contaminated and must carry that caveat. Whisper has no such exposure we know of.

Bare आधार and पैन are unusable outside government-task context. 3B-2 must either restrict the eval to government tasks, drop the bare variants, or add a context rule; the lexicon as it stands would count 'के आधार पर' as an Aadhaar mention.
recommendation: Use the government use-case tasks (6375 rows, 1386 pairs) as the Hindi entity arm, dev/test split by speaker_id; draw the clean (corruption) arm from non-government tasks.
